items.stem: An executive is triple-booked for 2 p.m.: a client renewal call, an internal 1:1, and a vendor demo. What is the best first action for the assistant?

options.text: Rank the three by business impact and deadline, then reschedule the lowest-priority with a proposed new time
options.rationale: Correct: triage by impact and urgency and move the least time-critical item while offering an alternative keeps commitments intact.

options.text: Decline all three and leave the slot free
options.rationale: Cancelling everything throws away commitments the executive may need to keep and solves nothing.

options.text: Let the executive discover the clash and decide in the moment
options.rationale: Surfacing the conflict late removes the chance to rebook gracefully and reflects poorly on the executive.

options.text: Attend one meeting yourself in the executive's place without asking
options.rationale: Standing in for the executive without authority oversteps the role and risks misrepresenting them.

items.explanation: Correct: triage by impact and urgency and move the least time-critical item while offering an alternative keeps commitments intact.

items.stem: Which practices keep a confidential reorganisation discreet while still doing the job well? (Select TWO)

options.text: Store related documents with restricted access and neutral file names
options.rationale: Correct: limiting access and avoiding revealing names reduces accidental disclosure.

options.text: Discuss only on a need-to-know basis and confirm what is shareable before acting
options.rationale: Correct: need-to-know plus confirming scope prevents premature leaks.

options.text: Mention the project casually to colleagues to gauge reaction
options.rationale: Fishing for reactions leaks confidential information and breaches trust.

options.text: Forward the planning thread to the whole team for transparency
options.rationale: Broad forwarding of confidential material is exactly the disclosure to avoid.

items.explanation: Correct: limiting access and avoiding revealing names reduces accidental disclosure.; Correct: need-to-know plus confirming scope prevents premature leaks.

items.stem: What distinguishes useful meeting minutes from a transcript?

options.text: Minutes capture decisions, owners and action items with dates
options.rationale: Correct: minutes exist so people know what was decided and who does what by when.

options.text: Minutes record every sentence spoken verbatim
options.rationale: A word-for-word record is a transcript; it buries the decisions readers actually need.
Attendance alone omits the decisions and actions that make minutes useful.

options.text: Minutes are the executive's private notes never shared
options.rationale: Minutes are shared so participants and absentees can act on the outcomes.

items.explanation: Correct: minutes exist so people know what was decided and who does what by when.
